source.title: Multimodal Large Language Model for Gloss-Free Video Sign Language Translation
source.authors: R. Guo; Xiaohui Hu; Tai-Ying Peng; Yao Du

record.tranche_reason: The study compares downstream sign-translation scores for 7B and 13B LLM backbones, a different measurement from the original pretraining-loss scaling studies.
record.gate_note: The paper cites scaling laws and reports improved translation scores when increasing its LLaMA backbone from 7B to 13B. It does not measure held-out pretraining cross-entropy, sweep training tokens or compute, fit scaling curves, or test a compute-optimal allocation. Rows capture the reported downstream scores for the two backbone sizes.
record.test_reason: In a new setting (LoRA-fine-tuned multimodal sign-language translation), the study compares LLaMA-2 7B and 13B backbones under otherwise identical training. This is a direct downstream scale comparison bearing on V6. It has only two sizes, so it cannot test predictability or curve shape.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors say the 7B→13B gain mirrors the scaling-law trend and infer that stronger base models give greater SLT gains. Their main conclusion, however, is that text-pretrained LLMs can learn sign-language visual grammar via Alignment-SFT with LoRA. Scaling is a side observation they do not test further.
record.recipe_differences: This is a fine-tuned multimodal sign-language translation study reporting downstream ROUGE and BLEU scores, rather than a scaling-law study fitting held-out pretraining loss against parameters, tokens, or compute.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports performance differences across datasets and model backbones, but does not assess sensitivity of a fitted scaling law or exponent.

fits_no_version.finding: At a fixed 7B size, swapping the pretrained backbone (Vicuna, Mistral, Qwen2, DeepSeek, Chinese-LLaMA) shifts CSL-Daily ROUGE by up to 4.3 points. That is comparable to the 7B→13B gain, and is language-dependent.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Downstream fine-tuned performance depends on base-model pretraining data and language match as much as on parameter count.

record.peer_reviewed: Information Technology and Control, Vol. 55, No. 1 (2026)
record.problems: The scale comparison uses only 7B and 13B backbones and reports downstream translation metrics, not held-out pretraining loss or a fitted scaling curve. The text reports no uncertainty estimates for these scores.

untested.parts: Predictability: only two sizes (7B, 13B), no fitted trend, no relation to pretraining loss, no token or compute variation.
No shape variation at fixed LLM parameter count; the visual-backbone ablation is not a loss test.
No power-law form in video or fine-tuning is tested; only two points.

missing.what: 7B vs 13B comparisons under ablated configurations: frozen LLM, linear or no-activation adaptor, and without LTN. Example: without LTN, Phoenix BLEU4 19.27 vs 21.43 and CSL 11.42 vs 13.34.
Fixed-size (7B) backbone comparison across five pretrained LLMs.

record.verdict_notes: The record's T2 is wrong: this is not a different method aimed at the same question, but a two-point downstream comparison in a new setting, so T3. There is a single run per configuration with no variance. The evidence for V6 is weak: it shows direction only. The labels are given for the direction of improvement, not for predictability.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out pretraining loss or power-law relationship in parameters, tokens, or compute is measured.
No small-run fits or predictions of larger runs are reported.
No fixed-compute allocation or compute-optimal parameter/token scaling is tested.
The visual-backbone ablations do not measure loss at fixed language-model parameter count, nor test the stated architecture claim.
The study uses video sign-language translation, but does not test whether a power-law form holds in this or another modality or training regime.
The study compares downstream translation scores at only two backbone sizes; it does not test predictability from pretraining loss or establish a general scale-performance curve.
No fitted exponents, fit choices, or departures from a single power law are examined.

relationships.condition: SL-LLaMA with LoRA-fine-tuned LLM (full configuration), PHOENIX-2014T and CSL-Daily test sets, 7B vs 13B
relationships.reason: Every reported metric is higher at 13B, e.g. BLEU4 20.86→23.73 on Phoenix and 11.77→13.42 on CSL-Daily (r1-r7). This shows the direction only, at two sizes.
relationships.display_finding: Every reported metric improved, with BLEU4 rising from 20.86 to 23.73 on PHOENIX-2014T and from 11.77 to 13.42 on CSL-Daily.

relationships.condition: Ablations with the LLM frozen, or with a non-GELU adaptor (Tables 3-4; no rows)
relationships.reason: From the text, not rows. With the LLM frozen, the 13B gain is small (BLEU4 15.95→16.52; 16.12→16.42). With an MLP adaptor without activation, 13B ROUGE barely moves (40.07→40.15). So the scale benefit depends on fine-tuning setup.
relationships.display_finding: With the language model frozen, scaling to 13B raised BLEU4 only from 15.95 to 16.52 and 16.12 to 16.42, while an adaptor without activation changed ROUGE only from 40.07 to 40.15.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
